00605.setting: Germline BRCA1/2-mutated, HER2-negative locally advanced/metastatic breast cancer after anthracycline/taxane or documented unsuitability; HR-positive disease requires prior endocrine therapy or unsuitability.

schedule.text: Talazoparib 1 mg orally once daily continuously until progression or unacceptable toxicity. A 28-day display is only a review block, never a tablet break.

administration.text: Swallow capsules whole; do not open or dissolve. Take with or without food.
Do not replace a missed or vomited dose; take the next prescribed dose at its usual time.

monitoring.text: Baseline: validated germline BRCA1/2 and HER2-negative confirmation, FBC, renal and liver profile, pregnancy test where applicable.
During treatment: FBC, renal and liver profile every four weeks or as clinically indicated; consider repeat pregnancy testing as indicated.
Disease monitoring follows the individual consultant treatment plan; no fixed scan interval is mandated here.

supportive_care.text: Minimal-to-low emetic potential; no routine premedication or other routine support specified. Use individual rescue antiemetic instructions.
Blood/platelet transfusion and growth-factor support are clinical options for myelosuppression, not automatic routine prescriptions.

drug_interactions.text: Avoid strong P-gp inhibitors; if unavoidable, reduce to the next lower current dose after review. On stopping the inhibitor, wait 3–5 inhibitor half-lives before restoring the pre-inhibitor dose.
Avoid strong BCRP inhibitors; if unavoidable monitor increased adverse effects.

contraception.text: Female patients: effective non-hormonal contraception during treatment and at least seven months afterwards; male patients: effective contraception during treatment and at least four months afterwards.
Avoid breastfeeding during treatment and at least one month after the last dose.

body_map.label: Blood counts / infection / bleeding
body_map.text: Fever, unusual bruising, bleeding, breathlessness or worsening fatigue need urgent advice.

body_map.label: Stomach / bowel
body_map.text: Report persistent nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea or poor fluid intake.

body_map.label: Energy / headache
body_map.text: Fatigue, dizziness or headache may affect daily activity; tell the team if new or worsening.

body_map.label: Hair
body_map.text: Hair thinning or loss can occur.

clinician_cautions: Renal impairment changes the recommended starting dose; toxicity and interactions still require review of the current prescription.
Breast monotherapy uses 1/0.75/0.5/0.25 mg dose levels; do not import lower prostate-combination capsule strengths.
Prior-treatment count toxicity should recover to grade ≤1 before initiation.
MDS/AML is rare but persistent cytopenia requires investigation.

00720.setting: Extended adjuvant treatment of HR-positive, HER2-positive early breast cancer, beginning less than one year after adjuvant trastuzumab completion.

schedule.text: Neratinib 240 mg (six 40 mg tablets) once daily continuously for one year unless progression or unacceptable toxicity. Dose reductions and interruptions follow the prescribed plan.

administration.text: Take with food, preferably in the morning; swallow whole, do not crush or dissolve.
Do not replace missed doses; resume the next scheduled daily dose.

monitoring.text: Baseline FBC, renal and liver profile; cardiac function/LVEF if clinically indicated. Eligibility includes normal baseline LVEF.
FBC monthly for the first six months, then every three months or as clinically indicated.
LFTs at week one, monthly for the first three months, then every six weeks during treatment or as clinically indicated.
Cardiac/LVEF assessment as clinically indicated, especially with cardiac risk. Do not impose a routine trastuzumab-style three-month schedule.
Severe diarrhoea requiring IV fluids or liver symptoms prompts extra liver and renal/electrolyte assessment.

supportive_care.text: Start anti-diarrhoeal prophylaxis with the first neratinib dose; adjust to one or two bowel movements daily.
NCCP loperamide schedule: weeks 1–2, 4 mg three times daily; weeks 3–8, 4 mg twice daily; weeks 9–52, 4 mg as needed. Additional therapy or neratinib interruption may be required.
Minimal-to-low emetogenic potential; routine antiemetic premedication is usually not required.
Hydration/diet plan and prompt escalation for diarrhoea are essential. The source suggests around two litres per day during diarrhoea; individual cardiac/renal restrictions take priority.

drug_interactions.text: Avoid grapefruit and pomegranate, and review CYP3A4/P-gp inhibitors/inducers and narrow therapeutic-index substrates.
Proton-pump inhibitors are not recommended because reduced absorption can reduce neratinib exposure. Do not add a generic supportive-care PPI.
With an H2 blocker, take neratinib at least two hours before or ten hours after it. Separate antacids by at least three hours.

contraception.text: Avoid pregnancy; effective contraception during treatment and for one month after stopping. Breastfeeding is excluded during therapy.

body_map.label: Diarrhoea / dehydration
body_map.text: Diarrhoea often starts early. Follow the written prevention plan and call promptly if it persists, fluids are difficult, or you become dizzy or unwell.

body_map.label: Liver
body_map.text: Report yellow eyes/skin, dark urine or right-sided upper abdominal pain; blood tests can detect problems before symptoms.

body_map.label: Skin / nails
body_map.text: Report troublesome rash, dry skin or nail changes.

body_map.label: Heart / breathing
body_map.text: New breathlessness, chest symptoms or swelling needs prompt assessment.

body_map.label: Mouth / appetite
body_map.text: Mouth soreness, nausea or poor intake may need support.

clinician_cautions: NCCP Child-Pugh C 33% and severe-renal/dialysis no-adjustment wording conflict with EMA restrictions; withhold automatic recommendations and resolve with oncology/pharmacy.
Exactly two days of grade 3 diarrhoea overlaps source rows; source count delay uses AND, not OR.
CONTROL dose escalation is tolerability evidence, not the NCCP v2 starting schedule. Do not replace routine source instructions without local adoption.
Late adjuvant surveillance and prior trastuzumab cardiac follow-up continue according to their own plans; neratinib does not reset them.
